Items.Title: Connection
Items.Description: Cloud preserves Owner/Fleet access. Gateway uses the customer HTTPS API. Signed LAN uses a separately registered driver key. Both local connections use your home network over Ethernet or Wi-Fi.

Items.Title: Use Cloud History with Local Access
Items.Description: Optional. Enable only with separate Owner/Fleet credentials and the numeric site ID belonging to this local system. Disabled means no cloud activity from a local driver.

Items.Title: Local Hostname or IP Address
Items.Description: Required for local access. A DNS hostname follows DHCP address changes. Optional HTTPS port; omit https://.

Items.Title: Local Password
Items.Description: Gateway and Signed LAN: local customer password. This is not your Tesla account password.

Items.Title: Registered Local Signing Key
Items.Description: Signed LAN only. Paste the private key from the driver local setup tool after registration and physical verification. Keep this credential private.

Items.Title: Allow Local Setting Changes
Items.Description: Local access is read-only by default. True permits the existing reserve, mode and supported grid settings.

Items.Title: Local Polling Interval Seconds
Items.Description: Delay after each completed local refresh. Defaults to 15 seconds. Requests do not overlap; slow requests extend the time between updates.

Items.Title: Tesla Fleet API Client ID
Items.Description: Optional. Leave blank to use the Tesla Owner API. Enter a Tesla Fleet API application Client ID to use the Tesla Fleet API instead; when set, the refresh token below must be a Fleet API refresh token, and Storm Watch is unavailable. Changing this value (adding, removing, or replacing it) invalidates the cached refresh token; a new refresh token for the new mode must be entered at the same time.

Items.Title: Tesla Refresh Token
Items.Description: OAuth refresh token for the Tesla account, obtained using an external setup tool. This is an Owner API refresh token unless a Client ID is also provided above, in which case it must be a Fleet API refresh token. The library automatically obtains and renews the access token from this refresh token on every connection; the driver updates this value here if Tesla rotates it. Note: changing the Client ID above invalidates this cached value, so a matching new refresh token must be entered whenever the Client ID is added, removed, or changed. Optional when local access is selected; leave blank for no cloud activity.

Items.Title: Tesla Energy Site ID
Items.Description: Optional. Enter the numeric Tesla energy site ID, or the site's name exactly as shown in the Tesla app/account (the driver looks up the matching ID automatically). Leave blank to use the account's first/default energy site. With local access and optional cloud history, the numeric ID for this exact physical site is required; no default-site selection is made.

Items.Title: Cloud Refresh Interval Seconds
Items.Description: Delay after a completed cloud refresh. With local access, this applies only to optional cloud history; local status uses its separate interval.
